    Public readiness audit — 2026-10-30

    Source: MAINTENANCE.md

    Base: 89bb9c2a0b7480414e375db4a89097143e32c846, in an isolated worktree. The original checkout and other working sessions are preserved. This package wraps the Cubert SDK for session enumeration, calibrated cube extraction and export. A working stub installation is useful for dependency resolution, but cannot establish SDK runtime, camera or scientific calibration correctness.

    Baseline

    R 4.6.1 on macOS ARM64, SDK absent: R CMD check --as-cran completed with 0 errors, 0 warnings and 2 notes in 38.8 seconds. Tests report 126 passing assertions and 23 skipped SDK/sample-data tests. Notes identify a bundled linked worktree .git file and the non-portable /bin/bash configure shebang. The current upstream hosted checks are successful; they do not verify the maintenance branch or provide evidence for the skipped SDK tier.

    The vendor’s public 3.6.1 Linux package was downloaded for header inspection only, not installed or executed. Its SHA-256 matches the vendor checksum: 64de880e06b90a97b92fd0eca9c9d3a0dc320deab72f92307c6a89a9b3a39f60. All five native source files pass a syntax check against that header. Warnings are retained (vendor comments/qualifier and standard R registration casts). The vendor release supplies Linux/Windows binaries, not a macOS runtime.

    Findings and implementation strategy

    1. High, native lifecycle: rcuvis_get_handle() permits access after SDK shutdown. R initialization also permits restarting a shutdown SDK or changing settings while initialized. The vendor header explicitly allows initialization only once; the existing SDK test contradicts its own warning and restarts it. Enforce initialization/retirement boundaries and canonical settings identity; test failure paths in isolated processes and keep real SDK qualification open.
    2. High, buffer integrity: cube conversion ignores buffer byte count, element size and null data, and calculates source offsets using signed int products. Check dimensions/format/length before allocation and use wide offsets. Verify all four formats and malformed buffers against a clearly synthetic native fixture; this is wrapper validation, not vendor runtime validation.
    3. High, export completion: the SDK documents asynchronous cube writing, but the wrapper did not flush or promptly release exporters. Explicitly flush before success and close on both success and error. The zero-initialized queue capacity also contradicts the SDK buffer contract; reserve one slot for the single measurement and disable dropping explicitly. A real-SDK deadlock was not reproduced on this unsupported host; exercise the actual R-to-C export path with synthetic responses and propagate flush failures.
    4. High, export preservation: session export unconditionally enables native overwrite. Export paths are silently truncated to CUVIS_MAXBUF - 1; logical options accept missing or nonscalar values. Require explicit overwrite intent, reject unsafe scalar/path inputs, document the migration and test that invalid requests do not reach SDK calls or alter existing files.
    5. Medium, SDK discovery: Unix configure can select a header without a usable library, ignores the conventional /usr/include installation, and substitutes paths through sed without escaping them. Windows discovery/link configuration needs equivalent missing-library checks. Make explicit SDK selection fail clearly; preserve deliberate stub installation when no SDK is requested.
    6. Medium, sample identity: named sample lookup treats literal filenames as regular expressions, so test_mesu.cu3s can select a different filename. Validate a scalar basename and match it literally without changing source data.
    7. Packaging/docs: exclude worktree metadata, use portable shell syntax, distinguish linked SDK from usable runtime, update vendor installation links and document exact first-use and restart behavior. Verify citation metadata before presenting a DOI as a published release.

    Acceptance: clean stub build/install/check; meaningful R and native boundary regressions; vendor-header compilation; validated configure scenarios; coherent manuals/examples and a runnable first-use path. Preserve calibration semantics and enumeration values. Camera/real .cu3s processing, Windows/Linux runtime, hosted CI and publication remain separate, explicitly unverified release gates.

    Verification

    Final source package cuvis.r_0.1.1.9000.tar.gz: SHA-256 9fdadf39848b83f66d6281783696798374decd19e6196ccc2ee4968c83cc37ba. On R 4.6.1/macOS ARM64, the full R CMD check --as-cran completed with 0 errors, 0 warnings, 1 note (new submission/development version).

    • R suite: 88 cases, 182 passing assertions, no failures/errors/warnings; 22 skips require a real SDK/sample recording or Windows runtime.
    • Native fixture: 143 checks pass against the vendor 3.6.1 header, including all four cube formats, malformed buffers, integer/string/logical inputs, post-shutdown handles, explicit overwrite, positive queue capacity, flush, immediate close and a flush failure through the actual R export function.
    • Configure: five tests pass. POSIX shell checks, actionlint and diff checks pass. The house linter retains 13 pre-existing report-only style findings.
    • Clean library: the exact archive installs with automatic stub detection; availability/version queries and SDK-unavailable initialization behave as documented, without creating the requested settings directory on failure.
    • Package inspection: 128 members, 72 source/manual/test/tool files match the checkout byte-for-byte; DESCRIPTION fields match after normal R build normalization. No worktree .git file or vendor/compiled binaries are bundled.
    • Documentation: pkgdown builds; 38 HTML pages and 1,221 local references have no missing targets. Eight browser assertions pass with no JavaScript errors; desktop and mobile screenshots were captured and the mobile page inspected.

    The first post-edit checks exposed an absent checkbashisms tool, a redirected vendor URL and an unparseable NEWS heading. These were corrected and checks repeated. The initial native harness lacked the SDK’s macro-declared metadata allocation symbols; that harness failure was fixed before native results were accepted. Pandoc emits deprecated-option notices during site generation; the site completes. Vendor header comment warnings are retained in native logs.

    Detailed logs and verification.json are in the workspace audit evidence folder for cuvis.r. The original checkout remains clean at the recorded base. No vendor binary was executed, no private source recording accessed, and no release, hosted workflow or deployment was performed for these changes.

    Release roadmap and remaining gates

    • Essential wrapper repairs: lifecycle, native buffer integrity, literal sample identity, export preservation and SDK discovery are implemented. Synthetic fixtures must keep rejecting invalid inputs without native memory access.
    • Dependable use: install the final source package in a clean library, verify stub first use, run the complete R check, and verify manuals/site navigation. The README records the intentional overwrite change and process restart rule.
    • Supported-host qualification: on Linux and Windows, install SDK 3.6.1 plus the applicable calibration and a complete exportable .cu3s fixture. Run the SDK test tier, compare raw/reflectance results with the vendor tools, reopen ENVI, TIFF and session exports, and verify paths/runtime dependencies. SDK errors now fail the export test rather than being silently converted into skips. No real-runtime or scientific-validity claim follows from the synthetic tier.
    • Publication: run hosted checks on the reviewed branch, choose the release version and confirm the package/release target, then publish only with authorization. Zenodo record 21889930 and its DOI both returned HTTP 404 on 2026-10-30; draft metadata remains, without a claimed published DOI.
    • Deferred: replace 13 existing stopifnot() style findings with a consistent public condition-class scheme in a separate compatibility-reviewed change. The house lint workflow remains report-only as before. No speculative camera acquisition, visualization or parallel processing features were added.

    Windows DLL dependencies must be discoverable on PATH before R starts. The package’s path-discovery helper is tested in isolation; this is not proof of a successful Windows DLL load. After SDK shutdown, restart R rather than unloading and reloading the package. Concurrent exports to one directory are unsupported.

    Runnable first use

    Requirements: R >= 4.1, a C compiler and the R dependencies declared in DESCRIPTION. From this checkout, a supported SDK host sets CUVIS_SDK before installation and CUVIS_SETTINGS before initialization. Windows also needs the SDK runtime bin directory on PATH before R starts. macOS can validate only the stub on the currently published SDK platforms.

    Rscript -e 'install.packages(c("cli", "rlang"))'
CUVIS_STUB=1 R CMD INSTALL .
Rscript -e 'library(cuvis.r); stopifnot(!cuvis_available())'
python3 tools/test-configure.py
python3 tools/test-native.py /path/to/vendor/cuvis.h

    For actual recordings, install without CUVIS_STUB after configuring the vendor SDK. Follow the README calibration example with the correct factory calibration and references, use an empty export directory, and shut down only after the whole batch. The immediate next release action is supported-host qualification and comparison with vendor output; publication is not authorized by this audit.
